note: Read by scripts/manual_capture.py. The CLOSED lists of what a manual-agent capture may do (FR-13): the step words of a `ui --steps-file` with their argument counts, the phases of a capture and the old words records written before the rename still carry (`phase_aliases`: the ONE source of the phase words - manual_capture.py, manual_evidence.py and grammar.py all read it), the HTTP methods, the headers that are never stored, and the default login recipe. A project replaces the recipe in qa-factory/config.json under `manual_capture.login.<ui|http>` (a present key replaces that kind whole, an absent one keeps this default, `null` means that kind needs no login); it never edits this file. The HTTP login is taken from the project's record in this order (manual_capture.http_login_source): its own `manual_capture.login.http`; else `environment.access` of kind `local_login` with a `url` (the address it records, the token read by name from the answer); else, only when the project records no access at all, this default. `environment.access.kind` `none` means no login by code and nothing is sent; `harness_command`, `bearer_env`, `oidc_password` or an unknown kind with no `manual_capture.login.http` refuse before any request, naming the key to record. `login.http` without `body` logs in with the body field names of `environment.access.user_field` / `secret_field`, else the pairs of references/login-body-fields.json in order; a project recipe with its own `body` is sent as written. `login.ui.landed` says how code proves the login landed: the URL contains none of `url_not`, and the cookie `session_cookie` exists, or, with no cookie named, the username field is gone. One step per line of the steps file, tokens split as a shell would (quote a selector or text that holds a space); blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored. A step word is handled by code, so a new word is a code change with its own test, not a data edit.

goto.does: open a full URL on a stand host named in config environments[]; the first goto of the file names the stand of the session

fill.does: make the field hold exactly the text, as a person does: clear the field (select all, delete), then key the text one character at a time with `manual_capture.type_delay_ms` between characters, record the field's value and focus after each character, then once more after `manual_capture.settle_ms`; an empty text only clears the field; a text that would take longer than the step limit at that pace is refused before any key is sent (door: `fill --whole`); `fill --whole <selector> <text>` and a field that cannot be keyed (a type of `whole_types`, a tag of `whole_tags`) set the whole value at once and say `input: whole` in the step line; never a credential - an account goes in with `fill-account`; a text that looks like a secret is keyed all the same but its log is not stored

fill-account.does: type the account's name (user) or password (secret) into the field; the actor is a form of `--as` (default, a role, env:USER_KEY/SECRET_KEY, created:<name>) and the value is read by code, never written in the steps file; the screen is not saved from the first such step until the page leaves the sign-in address

fill-new-account.does: make a NEW account through the app's own sign-up form, on a stand whose config row records `safe_to_break`: `user` generates the pair, records it (under a lock, before anything is typed) and types the name, shaped by the template (the data row `generated_user_template`, default `{generated_username}`; give `{generated_username}@example.test` when the form validates an email; a template without `{generated_username}` is refused); `secret` types the same pair's password and needs a `user` step before it in the item; the value is never written in the steps file, the log or the answer (they say `created:<name> [generated]`); the screen is not saved from the first such step until the page leaves the sign-in address; if the app refuses the sign-up (a later step fails while the page is still on the form) the account is recorded `unconfirmed` and is never used as `--as created:<name>`

account.does: say whether an account works: `confirmed` when you saw the app accept it (a created user that landed on the same address), `unconfirmed` when you created or were given it and could not confirm it works; the why quotes what you saw (one quoted argument, at most `why_max` characters, never a credential); the handle is a form of `--as` (default, a role, env:USER_KEY/SECRET_KEY, created:<name>); the step acts on nothing in the browser and records the word, the why and the page's path

look.does: look at the page the way a person does: store what the page shows (the accessibility tree of the whole page, or of the element when a selector is given; the page's text when the tree cannot be read) as a state file the role may cite; the first line of the file says which form it is (`form: aria`, `form: text (<why>)`); a tree longer than `max_bytes` is cut at a line with the cut named (`look <selector>` narrows it); refused inside the sign-in window

watch.does: from now on, until the end of the call, read the text of the element after every step; a change on a step that is no action is a `surprise` line; an element that is gone reads `<gone>`; at most `max_watched` watches per call

type.does: focus the field once,then key the text one character at a time with the pause between characters, and record the field's value and whether it still has focus after each character, then once more after `settle_ms`; a string a person types in a row is ONE call: a second `type` on the same field with no action between (a passive step - `keeps_run`: a read, a look, a wait - is not an action, as a person who looks does not click) goes on with the typing and does NOT set the focus again - when the field lost it, the keys go where the focus is and the step is not ok (`focus lost before the call: keys went to <what has focus>`); a `click` on the field between two calls is the person's own new click; use it when a field's value goes to the server or redraws the page (`fill` sets the whole value at once and hides a lost character or a lost focus); a text longer than max_chars is `fill`

press.does: focus the field and press one key from `keys` (or one printable character); records the field's value and its focus, and whether it had focus before the step; right after a `type` on the same field it goes on without a new focus (a person does not click again to press Enter), and a field that lost the focus is told as `focus lost before the call`

paste.does: focus the field and insert the text at once (an `input` event, not a `paste` event); records the field's value and its focus; right after a `type` on the same field it goes on without a new focus, as `press` does

fail_request.does: from now on every browser request of the page that matches the glob gets the status (an empty JSON body) or is dropped as timed out; it does not reach the stand; a glob with a host must name a stand host; a request sent by the page's server is not seen

restore_request.does: stop failing the requests of the glob; its result (`requests failed: N`) is written to the evidence, and a restored rule no longer holds a `capture post_action`; a rule never lifted ends with the walk item that declared it

end-session.device: none: a device has no such step (`app_steps` lacks it), the steps file of a device naming it is refused with the device's own list
end-session.does: delete every cookie of the browser context of the current actor, as a session that ran out; the page stays open as it was, and the next request of the page goes without the session cookie; the answer says how many cookies were deleted - `0 cookies` when the context held none (a guest, an actor not signed in, a second `end-session` in a row), which is a no-op said aloud, not a failure; no cookie name or value is stored

drag.does: press on the element, move the mouse by dx, dy pixels (whole numbers), release

wait.does: a whole number is milliseconds; anything else waits for the selector to appear

read.does: store the value (text by default) in a log file and in the step line; this is how a viewport transform or a status text is read; an attribute the element lacks reads as read_absent_marker, an empty one as nothing; state= is true or false for one of read_states; `expect=<text>` (the LAST argument) is the role's own planned value: the value read is compared with it, whitespace collapsed, and the step line says `expect: matched` or `expect: differs` (the step row carries `expect`); a walk call stops on a difference, a `ui` call only records it; the code compares bytes and never says who is right

capture.does: take a screenshot now; the label names the file and is what the capture proves: `capture post_action completion` is the one line that proves the completion condition was reached

http.does: one HTTP request on the walk's stand, sent as the request's actor; walk only. A path (`/v1/x`) is joined to the stand's base_url, a full URL must be on the walk's stand; the body file is given as an absolute path written with forward slashes (a backslash is an escape in a step line) and holds no generated-value placeholder; the request and the answer are stored as one JSON document (a capture the role may quote), and a 3xx, 4xx or 5xx answer is a `surprise` line (a redirect is not followed)

launch.does: bring the app under test to the front of the device

fill.does: clear the field and type the text into it; never a credential - an account goes in with `fill-account`

fill-account.does: type the account's name (user) or password (secret) into the field; the value is read by code, never written in the steps file; the screen is not saved from the first such step until the sign-in screen is gone (config manual_capture.login.app.sign_in_selector names an element only the sign-in screen has)

drag.does: press on the element, move by dx, dy pixels (whole numbers), release

wait.does: a whole number is milliseconds; anything else waits for the element to appear

read.does: store the element's text (by default) or one attribute in a log file and in the step line; an attribute the element lacks reads as read_absent_marker

source.does: store the screen's element tree (XML) as a state file, hidden from the session's accounts and scanned for secrets; a quote of a Then may come from it

look.does: the same as `source`: store the screen's element tree as a state file (a device has no page text to narrow it by, so a selector is refused: `look` without an argument)

log.does: store the tail of the device's log as a log file (a surface whose row has no log refuses it)

capture.does: take a screenshot of the device now; the label names the file and is what the capture proves

capture_surfaces.note: Which test profile of the project a capture is about (manual_capture.capture_profile), closed variety so data (FR-13). `capabilities`: a profile that lists one of these words fits the surface; `level`: a profile whose id equals it fits too, and it is the plan level (contract.PLAN_LEVELS) whose runtime_probes entry an older config keeps by that word. `--profile <id>` always wins and must be a profile of config.json. `table_free`: a project whose every capability is such a word, and that names no `surface`, never reads references/surfaces.json (scripts/surfaces.py `declared_surfaces`).

app.limitation: network of the device is not confined to the stand

capture_words.profile_unknown: --profile {asked!r} is not a profile of config.json. Expected one of: {names}
capture_words.profile_several: several test profiles fit this {surface} capture ({names}): name one with --profile
capture_words.profile_none: no test profile of config.json fits this {surface} capture. Expected --profile <id> naming one of profiles[], or a profile in profiles[] whose capabilities list {capabilities}
capture_words.browser_door: Playwright cannot be imported here ({why}). Install it for the Python that runs the factory (python -m pip install playwright, then python -m playwright install chromium), then capture again.
capture_words.failure_host: `fail_request` pattern {glob} names the host {host}, which is not a configured stand. Expected a pattern with no host (`**/api/x`) or one on a stand host: {hosts}
capture_words.failure_unmet: no request matched {globs} in this session, so this page has not met the failure. Load or repeat the action that sends the request (goto, click, wait) while the failure is on, or correct the pattern in a new attempt. The request may be sent by the page's server, where a browser route cannot see it: then this level cannot make the failure, and the check needs another level.
capture_words.failure_idle: fail_request {glob} matched no request in this session: the page never met the failure
capture_words.session_ended: {n} {unit} deleted: this actor's browser context no longer holds the session; the page stays open as it was
capture_words.session_none: 0 cookies: this actor's browser context held none (nobody was signed in here, or the session was already ended); nothing changed
capture_words.failure_star_hint: hint: in the pattern {glob} a single `*` does not cross `/`, so it matches one path segment only; for any host write `**/api/x`
capture_words.requests_none: no request to a stand host was seen in this call: the log lists the browser's own requests only (a request sent by the page's server is not seen), so zero here is not 'the page sends none' - record a `coverage_gap` if the cells depend on it
capture_words.harness_none: no test profile that fits a `ui` capture has a command that runs `pytest`, so no other interpreter that has Playwright can be derived from config.json. {door}
capture_words.harness_unstarted: the harness interpreter could not be started ({head}: {error}). It is the command up to `pytest` of the test profile that fits a `ui` capture, run in {folder}. {door}

stand_lease.does: a `ui`, `http` or `app` call waits this many seconds for a stand another job holds, then answers `stand_busy` (exit 3); a project overrides it with `run.manual_stand_wait_s`. Short on purpose: a role's shell call is ended by its host long before the suites' `run.stand_wait_s`

requests_seen.unlogged: the requests this page sent are not logged by this capture backend (a device has no browser requests): the cells of the exploration charter come from the code only, so a request the code scan missed is a gap - record it as a `coverage_gap`, never read it as 'the page sent none'
requests_seen.does: at the end of a `ui` call the browser requests of the page to a stand host are stored as `requests-seen.txt` in the attempt: `METHOD address` (no query), one line per distinct pair with `xN` for a repeat, at most `max_logged` lines and a `... and K more` line; a line that matches a secret pattern is counted, not kept

surprise.limitation: the surprise detector sees the main page's requests to a stand host, their answers, failed requests, console errors and page errors; it does not see websockets, event streams, service workers, requests the page's server makes, or a new tab: an empty list is not 'nothing happened' there
surprise.note: The words of the steps after which the call waits for the page to quiet down (`settle`: `settle_ms`, then the network idle, held to the step's remaining limit and to `settle_idle_max_ms`): an event the step caused reaches the step that caused it, never the next one. `action_steps` change the page by design, `input_steps` type into it

walk_session.does: A step call of `walk_session.py step` holds 1..max_batch_steps steps, one per line, in the step words above (one step is a call of one; nothing prefers or requires a batch). The server runs them in order on the kept page and stops at the first deviation: a step whose outcome is not ok (always, `--stop-on` cannot switch it off), a `read ... expect=` that read otherwise, a surprise line of the step that matches a stop rule, or the call's time budget spent between steps (batch_time). A stop is not a verdict: it says what happened and the role decides. The default stops on a 5xx the role did not cause, a console or page error and a navigation no step asked for, because the page is then in a state the plan did not foresee and the next planned step would act blind; it does not stop on a 4xx or a value the application changed while typing, because a negative step is sent to provoke exactly those and the line is recorded and shown in the answer either way. A call over max_batch_steps is refused whole before any step runs, never cut. The lanes `settle` and `control` (`open --place`) are the failure analyst's: their session takes the stand lease for ONE request at a time (item, step, look, final, close, and the start) and waits for it at most request_lease_wait_s, then answers exit 3 stand_busy naming the holder, so the analyst's own test runs are never blocked by its session; and idle_s does not end them (idle_places_exempt): they end with the dispatch, its parent or max_s.

words.source_factory_default: the factory's default recipe, which this project never confirmed
words.not_known_line: login by code: this project's sign-in is not an HTTP request the factory knows (environment.access.kind {kind}); nothing was sent
words.not_known_door: a screen case signs in with fill-account steps, and a seed is done through the screens; for the project: record manual_capture.login.http in config.json (path and token_field), or null if this kind of capture needs no login
words.default_unconfirmed: login by code at {url} did not give a token ({status}). The address is the factory's default recipe, which this project never confirmed, so the stand has not judged the account: record manual_capture.login.http in config.json (path and token_field), or record the sign-in as environment.access of kind local_login with its url; say so in your findings
words.none_said: environment.access.kind is none: no login by code
